one_liner: Clinical case manager at DC's federal probation/parole agency who assesses offenders for mental health and substance use needs and places them in treatment programs.
fit_summary: This job requires a current independent clinical license (LISW, LICSW, LPC or comparable) plus a year of GS-11-level experience assessing and case-managing offenders with mental health and substance use disorders. Nothing on file shows Daniel holds such a license or clinical corrections experience. Daniel's emergency-management consulting, policy knowledge and people skills do not substitute for those requirements.
eligibility: Open to the public (also veterans and federal transition paths), so status is not required.
Selective Placement Factor: you must hold and upload a current independent social services license or certification (LISW, LICSW, LPC or comparable), or you will not be rated qualified.
Basic requirement: a bachelor's or higher degree in behavioral or social sciences (or 24 semester hours in them), with transcripts submitted, or an equivalent education/experience combination.

One year of specialized experience at the GS-11 level: intensive case management for offenders with mental illness, in-depth substance abuse assessments, and administering and interpreting screeners to make placement recommendations.
Security clearance listed as 'Other', so expect a background investigation; the job is on-site in DC with no telework.
strategy: First confirm whether you hold an LISW, LICSW, LPC or comparable certification. If not, skip this posting, because applying without the license will be screened out automatically.
Use this posting to learn where CSOSA hires non-clinical staff instead, such as program analyst, community relations or policy roles. Those jobs better match your IEM and public policy background.
If you are licensed, put the license number, state and expiration date at the top of your two-page resume, and upload the license and transcripts before October 30, 2026.

Translate any IEM work with vulnerable populations or service referrals into case management language only if it is true. Do not stretch emergency-management consulting into clinical experience on the questionnaire.

Prepare for the USA Hire assessment, which has a cut score. Rest beforehand, set aside uninterrupted time, and answer the situational items honestly to show teamwork, stress tolerance and customer service.
resume_bullets: Conducted [number] substance use and mental health assessments using [tool, e.g., ASAM/LSI-R], developing integrated treatment plans and referrals for [population] ([hours]/week, [dates]).
Provided case management for a caseload of [number] court-involved clients, monitoring compliance with treatment and medication requirements and reporting progress to [supervision officers/courts].
Coordinated with [agencies/partners] at IEM to connect [disaster-affected residents/clients] with social services, tracking outcomes in [system] and producing weekly status reports.
interview_questions: Walk us through how you administer and score a risk-needs assessment and turn the results into a placement recommendation.
How do you apply risk-needs-responsivity principles when choosing an intervention for a high-risk offender?
Describe a time you disagreed with a supervision officer or team member about a client's plan. How did you resolve it?
How do you maintain clinical files and meet quality-assurance standards under heavy caseload pressure?
watch_outs: The independent clinical license is mandatory, and you appear not to have one, so this posting is likely a non-starter.
You must show one year of clinical corrections experience at the GS-11 level, which your consulting background does not show.
The job is fully on-site in DC with no telework, which means a long daily commute from Manassas.
The position has no promotion potential beyond GS-12.
